title: Tiebreaker heuristic notes for Senior Runtime role - Jasmin Ko
content:
Context / purpose:
Quick personal write-up to help resolve the split votes for the Senior Runtime Engineer loop. This is intentionally a messy, fast riff — meant to surface heuristics I keep returning to when we’re balancing product fit vs risk. Use as a tiebreaker, not as a checklist.

High-level gut verdict (2-sentence):
Candidate is technically solid on model serving fundamentals and has good instincts about tail-latency mitigation. I am leaning hire-with-conditions (small onboard ramp plan + pair for 4 weeks on kernel-level optimizations) because the behavioral signals are mixed but remediable.

Where we agreed (summary):
- Strong: async batching strategy, KV cache tradeoffs, concrete examples of performance debugging (tracing flamegraphs -> kernel hotspots).
- Strong: pragmatic about operational tradeoffs (prefers incremental rollout, blue/green + canary defaults).
- Red flags raised by panel: sketchy infra ownership history (short stints), slightly hand-wavy on cross-team communication examples.

Tiebreaker heuristics I used (explicit so others can poke them):
1) Can they land a 90-day technical plan with measurable wins? If yes -> hire. We care about throughput/latency wins quickly. Candidate provided a 90-day plan in the pairing task (see notes below) with 3 measurable checkpoints: baseline perf, KV-cache hit-rate + 10% throughput, tail-latency 99.9 reduction by X ms. That concreteness carries weight.

2) Signal vs. noise in short-tenure history: look for artifacts, not narratives. If candidate has code/PRs showing ownership in 6–8 week sprints -> weight positive. There were 2 PRs shared that fixed scheduling bottlenecks; both small but atomic. I want one more artifact (perf regression PR or a postmortem) before final offer.

3) Communication under ambiguity: did they ask clarifying questions? In pairing they asked good instrumenting questions but didn’t proactively map stakeholder impacts (e.g., product owners, billing). That's a coachable gap. If other interviewers saw stronger stakeholder mapping -> tilt to hire; if they also saw fuzzy mapping -> tilt against.

Pairing notes (session with me, 60m):
- Task: diagnose rising 95/99 latencies for a sharded model endpoint after a quantization rollout.
- Steps: reproduced locally using synthetic traces, added tracing spans, isolated hot loop to attention kernel.
- Wins: proposed incremental rollback + runbook automation; sketched a fallback model routing policy for small-tenancy customers.
- Gap: initial proposal assumed affinity-based scheduling without calling out potential fragmentation effects on bin-packing and cost. Needed prompting to consider the cost-behavior tradeoff.

Behavioral/Leadership assessment (quick bullets):
- Motivations: wants to be in a place where they can influence infra decisions end-to-end (good).
- Cross-team: examples tended towards bilateral short-term wins ("I shipped X with infra team") rather than long-running alignment projects. Not bad, but we need someone who will push for runtime conventions across groups.
- Mentorship: gave a coherent approach to code reviews and onboarding, suggested pairing rotations (positive signal).

Risk map (what would make me change to no-hire):
- If we see repeated hand-wavy answers on durability/consistency edge cases (e.g., cache eviction races, sequence shuffle on streaming inputs) across other interviewers -> no hire.
- If background checks show pattern of leaving projects mid-delivery.
- If compensation expectations are > our top-of-band and candidate is not willing to accept a stretch offer with milestones.

Remediation plan if we hire (practical onboarding conditions):
- 0–30 days: focused onboarding on our tracing and perf infra. Buddy: Diego R. Pair twice/week for first 2 weeks on live incidents.
- 30–60 days: own one minor perf regression (measurable improvement + postmortem).
- 60–90 days: lead a lightweight rollout strategy for an internal feature (canary + automatic fallback).
Include clause in offer: if milestones not met, move to IC2 review before conversion to full responsibilities.

Comp / level recommendations (subjective):
- Level: Senior (IC4) — candidate meets the bar for technical depth and product thinking, but not clearly at Staff (IC5) yet.
- Comp posture: offer mid-to-upper band with growth milestone to unlock top band after 6 months of measurable wins.

Sample questions to follow-up in asynchronous thread (short, actionable):
1) Can you share a PR or postmortem where you fixed a production perf regression and describe the measurement baseline + deployment pattern? (artifact request)
2) Walk me through a specific instance where you had to align 3+ teams on a runtime change — what tactics did you use, what failed? (seeks concrete tactics)
3) Have you owned a KV cache semantics design before? What eviction policies did you choose and why? (pin down durability semantics)

Notes-to-self / unresolved instincts (raw):
- Candidate seems to prefer getting into the stack and shipping quick wins; might be less inclined to chase long-term platform design. That's not a deal-breaker, but we must match role responsibilities (we need someone who will steward platform patterns, not just fix fires).
- Ask hiring manager whether the immediate first-quarter project is more tactical or strategic. If tactical, candidate fits nicely. If strategic, push harder for Staff-level signals.

Action items (what I will do next):
- Request 1 artifact (PR or postmortem) and a brief written example of a multi-team alignment. Deadline: EOD + 3 business days.
- Sync with Maya to surface the tiebreaker and align the conditional offer language.
- If ok, propose hire-with-conditions: 6-month milestone-based uplift to top band.

Random micro-observations (notes to copy into panel thread):
- Good instinct for tracing placement (span granularity right).
- Suggested an interesting but risky optimization: prefilling KV cache from controller during idle windows — conceptually good but could add cold-start load if not gated. Mention as an area to test rather than immediate ship.

End.
